findings.evidence: Lines 314-321 vs 328-335: both are `have hab : a ≠ b := fun h => hne (congrArg …)`; `rcases hab.lt_or_gt with hlt | hlt`; `rcases (…_order … hne htail).mp hlt with h | h <;> simp only [h.1, ne_eq, reduceCtorEq, not_false_eq_true]`; then `have ht := fun j hj => (htail j hj).symm`, a `rw` of the tail at the next index, and the same `rcases … hne.symm ht`. `thomEncoding_apply` (line 103) is `(rfl)`, so `hne : thomEncoding p a i ≠ thomEncoding p b i` is `derivativeSign p a (i.val+1) ≠ derivativeSign p b (i.val+1)`, i.e. `thom_next_nonzero` at `k := i.val+1`, whose conclusion `derivativeSign p a (k+1)` is the goal. `grep -rn 'thom_next_nonzero\|thomEncoding_next_ne_zero' code/` matches only lines 309/313/324 in this file.
findings.fix: Move `thom_next_nonzero` above `thomEncoding_next_ne_zero` and replace the latter's body with an application of it at `k := i.val + 1`, reusing the shared tail-conversion lemma suggested below; `thomEncoding p a ⟨i.val + 1, _⟩ = derivativeSign p a (i.val + 1 + 1)` holds by `rfl`.

summary: The Thom encoding material is genuinely absent from Mathlib and TauCeti, and the Rolle, occCount/signCount, and Tarski-query APIs are reused correctly; both prior findings are fixed.
